A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Error Notebook-guided CAD part-retrieval work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval experiments across several VLMs, CoT/exemplar ablations, an image-only comparison and qualitative retrieval cases.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and adds grammar-filter evaluations, alternative baselines, open-source model results, retrieval metrics, retriever sensitivity and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The two-stage pipeline, reasoning correction and RAG procedure remain. V3 adds strict/relaxed notebook filtering based on answer markers and valid filenames (Section 2.4), a token-Jaccard retrieval alternative, and GPT-4o-generated notebooks for Qwen inference. These are bounded extensions to filtering, retrieval and exemplar sourcing.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate specification-driven part retrieval using the same Fusion 360 archive and its self-generated and human-preference datasets. New model configurations, retrieval variants and smaller evaluation subsets do not introduce another dataset domain or task.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated standard few-shot and self-consistency baselines in Table 3, substantially extending comparison beyond notebook removal and image-only reasoning. It also adds with/without-notebook comparisons for Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct and Aya-Vision-8B. The original proprietary-model comparators and image-only comparison remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include recall/F1 evaluation, self-consistency with five samples at temperature 0.7, and a 100-sample latency study using one endpoint, one worker and no batching. V3 also introduces 2B/8B model configurations and Aya evaluations on 666/370 cases. These supplement the retained original evaluation rather than establish changed settings for its unchanged results.

E4.justification: V3 tests strict versus relaxed filtering, notebook transfer from GPT-4o to Qwen, character versus token-based retrieval, and computational overhead. These address filter failure, exemplar quality, retrieval sensitivity and practicality. The original CoT/exemplar ablation, image-only comparison and twelve case studies remain; their relocation is not new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports seeds, confidence intervals or variability estimates. V3 mentions an additional Aya-Vision run on different hardware, but does not clarify whether it repeats the evaluation or covers additional computation. Thus, a change in repeated-evaluation reporting is ambiguous. Self-consistency's five samples are part of inference, not an uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: All original rows in Tables 1 and 2 are retained unchanged. V3 adds substantial results for filtering, baselines, open-source models, recall/F1, retrieval scoring and efficiency. For example, GPT-4o human-preference accuracy is 66.8% with sGC and 68.1% with token-level retrieval, versus the retained 65.1% notebook result. These are new variant results, not corrections to the original setting.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 adds an elementary API-call cost derivation: notebook construction requires the sum of each assembly's part count plus two calls per assembly (Equation 7). The original reasoning-trajectory and retrieval mathematics remain substantively unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions now claim additional gains from GC verification, superiority to standard few-shot and self-consistency, and effectiveness on open-source VLMs, including cross-model transfer approaching GPT-4o mini. Open-source integration changes from future work in v1 to a claimed demonstrated contribution in v3.

C2.justification: V3 explains strict filtering's failure on Qwen through rejection of otherwise acceptable traces, interprets cross-model notebooks as reasoning transfer, and argues for retrieval-score robustness and manageable overhead. Its latency explanation invokes improved coherence and reduced internal search as possibilities. V1's interpretation that Gemini 2.5 better aligns with human preferences is removed.

D1.justification: V3 discloses character-level retrieval scoring, open-source hardware/runtimes, baseline generation settings and token/API costs. It also identifies GPT-4o and prompt tailoring for the retained image-only ablation. Original prompts and core API details remain. Conversely, v1's reproducibility statement and promise to release code are removed; neither PDF supplies a code-access link.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for Qwen2-VL and Aya-Vision and explicitly positions the approach against alternative training-free inference strategies. The CAD survey and CAD-automation references have corrected author attributions but identify the same works. The broader CAD and self-correction positioning remains.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the abstract and contribution narrative, places problem formulation before dataset construction, expands the explanation of the two stages, and reorganizes the appendices around supplementary results and prompts. The LLM-use, ethics and reproducibility sections are removed. This is substantial structural revision beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: V3 adds a front-page scope diagram, combines the dataset and inference diagrams, redraws notebook construction to include GC, expands Table 1 and introduces several result tables. Original Figures 4–5 move unchanged to Figures A.1–A.2; engineering and case-study images are retained with relocation and layout changes.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens the empirical case by addressing v1's lack of alternative training-free baselines, testing filter and retriever choices, and measuring engineering costs. Open-source evaluations also replace a proposed extension with evidence. These gains outweigh reporting drawbacks: the abstract's roughly four-point GPT-4o-mini gap applies only to the fewer-than-ten-part human-preference subset against the unaugmented comparator, and the code-release commitment is dropped.
